3. Course Trajectories in the Didactic Space

We embed all courses from all 5 years and track how they move in the shared embedding space. Even courses with only names (2021–2023) occupy a semantic position that can be compared with the same course's richer representation in 2024–2025.

Multi-Year Course Trajectories (PCA)

Each point is a course in a specific year. Arrows connect the same course across consecutive years. Labeled items are long-lived courses with significant drift.

Trajectory Insight

Courses with the same name can drift substantially in embedding space when their description evolves. This "semantic drift" is invisible to traditional catalog analysis but measurable in the Didactic Space.

Embedding Similarity Distribution (2024→2025)

For courses present in both 2024 and 2025: distribution of cosine similarity between their embeddings. Higher = more stable content.

10. Methodology

What the Didactic Space Reveals

Traditional curriculum analysis compares names and credits. The Didactic Space adds semantic positioning: each course occupies a point in a 384-dimensional space, benchmarked against labor market demands, institutional mission, and peer curricula. Temporal tracking turns these points into trajectories, revealing:

  • Invisible drift: courses with the same name that shift content over time
  • Structural evolution: program-level changes in didactic composition
  • Objective realignment: curriculum moving toward or away from market/mission targets
  • Competency redistribution: how competency profiles adapt to new FGOS standards
